messages:
marie: Quick sync on the small-multiples grid in Console Model Insights. At narrow card widths (≈240px) the y-axis labels like `latency.p95_ms` wrap and cause row height jitter. Options I'm considering: always-abbreviate metric keys (e.g., `p95`), collapse axis to a left stub that expands on hover, or keep full text but force single-line with ellipsis + tooltip. Also: smoothing control (per-metric toggle vs global default) and anomaly handling (dim vs explicit marker). Thoughts?

sam: Screenshot would help but sounds familiar. Are the wraps coming from unit suffixes (`_ms`) or long metric namespaces?

marie: Mostly suffixes + percentile names. Namespace is short. Example label: `latency.p95_ms`. At 240px it wraps to two lines and cards look uneven in the grid.

alex: My preference: abbreviate visually but surface full semantics to assistive tech. Show `p95` + `ms` on one line. Use tooltip for the human-readable expansion: `95th percentile latency (p95) - milliseconds`. Avoid hover-only UX for keyboard users.

toni: Agree. If you abbreviate, include aria-labels like: `aria-label="95th percentile latency (p95) in milliseconds"`. Also ensure the left stub expansion is keyboard reachable (e.g., focusable region with Enter to expand).

marie: Good call. For compact axis states I'm leaning toward two-line strategy: "stub mode" shows short tokens (`p50`, `p95`) + unit on one line; expanded shows full key. Tooltip and aria-label provide full copy.

sam: That seems pragmatic. For copy, prefer short microcopy. For the smoothing control: label options? I prototyped: `Smoothing (reduce noise)` vs just `Smooth lines`.

alex: I like `Smoothing (reduce noise)` because it cues intent. Tooltip: `Use smoothing to reveal trends; disable to inspect raw spikes.`

marie: Noted. On outliers: we currently dim extreme points which some people think hides data. Suggestion: add a sentinel marker (diamond) + `Highlight anomalies` toggle. When on, markers are visible and keyboard-focusable; else we show no markers but keep dimming.

toni: Accessibility nit: don't rely on color alone. Use shape + outline + aria description. Example aria text per marker: `Anomaly on 2025-03-01 14:00: value 12.3 ms, ~3x baseline`. Also provide a data table view linked from the chart for screen-reader users.

sam: Good. Also add a short legend entry for the marker: `◇ anomaly (deviates from baseline)`. Legend copy should be concise.

alex: Implementation note for eng: expose per-metric smoothing toggle, but keep a global default in settings. Perf-wise, smoothing should be computed on the client with a stable algorithm (e.g., 3-point rolling median) to avoid server churn.

marie: Action items I'll take: (1) mock compact axis/stub + expanded state; (2) write microcopy for `Smoothing (reduce noise)` tooltip and `Highlight anomalies` tooltip + legend text; (3) sample aria-labels for axis labels and anomaly markers. Sam will file tickets for eng to add keyboard focus and per-metric smoothing flag.

sam: I'll open the ticket and include accessibility checklist.

ui-bot: Deploy preview link: https://staging.redwood.ai/console/insights/small-multiples?mock=compact-axes (expires in 24h)

marie: Thanks all ":thumbsup:" I'll post mocks in ~90m and include example aria snippets for review.

toni: Quick reminder: when you post aria examples please include how the screen reader will speak it (e.g., exact string). That makes reviews faster.
